name: Eisenhower Matrix
use_case: A two-by-two split of tasks by urgency and importance, producing four handling rules: do the urgent and important now, schedule the important but not urgent, delegate the urgent but unimportant, and delete the rest. Best used by an individual or a lead whose day is consumed by interruptions and who needs to see how little time is reaching the important-but-not-urgent quadrant where the durable work actually lives.
strengths: separates urgency from importance, which people routinely conflate
makes visible how little time reaches genuinely important work
applies to a personal task list, no team or meeting required
the delete quadrant gives explicit permission to drop things
weaknesses: importance is self-assessed and drifts toward whatever feels pressing
no notion of effort, dependency or sequence
delegation assumes someone to delegate to
suited to tasks, not to comparing large pieces of product work
